primary_goal: Build one cross-problem research agent that uses development-scope behavior profiles, discriminating counterexamples and falsifiable mechanism memory to choose one replayable scientific action per tick, then confirm, transfer or stop under frozen evidence rules.

core_thesis.name: Falsifiable Mechanism Ecology
core_thesis.falsification_boundary: If the four components do not change one another during replayed action selection, the system is not an FME closed loop.

research_questions.RQ1: Does active falsification outperform score-only or structured passive feedback under the same total evaluation budget?
research_questions.RQ2: Does evidence-scoped falsifiable mechanism memory outperform ordinary RAG or elite retrieval?
research_questions.RQ3: Can the same controller be re-instantiated across BP, TSP and CVRP using problem adapters and abstract mechanism transfer?
research_questions.RQ4: Does FME improve algorithm quality and research efficiency under comparable budgets?

implementation_phases.name: evidence_integrity_closure
implementation_phases.gate: freeze and close ORF-001 through ORF-005 before integration or cohort execution

implementation_phases.name: deep_fme_research_loop
implementation_phases.gate: deterministic no-LLM replay executes a non-generation action and stops

implementation_phases.name: adapter_convergence
implementation_phases.gate: problem-specific fields do not enter the controller interface and each ProblemAdapter rejects counterexamples outside frozen distance size or structural constraints

implementation_phases.name: evidence_memory_closed_loop
implementation_phases.gate: counterevidence changes a claim and the next replayed action

implementation_phases.name: offline_historical_replay
implementation_phases.gate: sample top-N random-N and all failed candidates per problem from the 605-run pool; profile the evaluation cascade and demonstrate unconstrained counterexample drift without an API call

implementation_phases.name: paired_bp_pilot
implementation_phases.gate: requires a new frozen v3 manifest and explicit remaining LLM budget; both arms use one fixed EOH generator and one fixed model so only FME control differs

implementation_phases.name: cross_problem_transfer
implementation_phases.gate: target claims restart as proposed and use independent target evidence

attribution.agent_contribution_requirement: actor=research_agent with a complete replayable decision chain

non_negotiable_rules: There is exactly one formal top-level scientific controller.
Each research tick executes one primary scientific action and writes a DecisionRecord.
Formal held-out evidence never enters ResearchState, prompts, retrieval, mechanism claims or next-action selection.
Failed, infeasible, timed-out, tied, missing and negative-transfer coordinates remain in evidence.
Cross-problem transfer carries abstract mechanisms and evidence boundaries, not source executable code or source held-out conclusions.
Counterexamples outside frozen problem-specific domain constraints remain failure evidence and cannot enter the accepted counterexample archive.
P5 uses one fixed EOH generator and one fixed model in both arms; the only treatment difference is FME controller activation.
Unconstrained counterexample generation is an offline P4 risk demonstration, not a P5 formal arm.
API availability does not imply budget authorization.
No test suite, full build, API call, LLM run or formal experiment is executed without the applicable explicit authorization.
Core execution does not depend on Codex, Obsidian, an absolute local path or one operating system.
